entries.value: Operator-adjustable SettingsFacts in the Aerora settings group, mirroring how maxCacheDiskSize drives tile pruning, with defaults of 365 days of age and 2 GB of total size across Events and EventValues. A year is chosen so that an annual audit, an insurance cycle and a full operating season all fall inside the window rather than outside it. 2 GB is large for integer and text rows and small against the disks these stations run on. Both are raised or lowered per deployment rather than compiled in, so a fleet flying constantly and a single aircraft flown weekly are configured rather than forked. Sessions follow Events and are pruned when no audit record references them. Vehicles are never pruned automatically: an operator deletes a vehicle record explicitly.

settled.element: whether an audit record may be deleted at all per D-DAT-02

entries.value: No. An audit record may not be deleted at all, by an operator or by the pruner, and may only be exported. This is already a database property rather than a rule the pruner has to remember, because AuditRecords uses ON DELETE RESTRICT while every other table uses CASCADE, so pruning a session cannot remove audit records as a side effect. The consequence for the interface is that the confirmation flow of SCR-SEC-03 is an export flow and not a delete flow. The reason is that an operator who can delete the record of their own actions leaves no evidence that they did, which defeats what the audit is for.

value.meaning: A link opened, closed, or changed Link_Class.
A vehicle appeared, was adopted into the fleet, or asserted a firmware claim.
A reported value changed its State_Vocabulary class. The one category that populates Events.stateClass; every other category leaves it null.
An operator acted through the interface.
A command was allowed or denied, with the role that authorised it.
A plan was uploaded, downloaded, cleared or resumed.
A payload capability or payload state changed as reported by the vehicle.
A station-side failure: a store write that failed, an audit record that was lost, a message that could not be parsed.
